name: William E. McLellin
role: Early missionary and apostle who later left the Church
dateNote: He was baptized in August 1831 and met Joseph Smith that October; he became an apostle in 1835 and was excommunicated in 1838.
importance: Section 66 answers five questions he had asked privately, and he wrote that it answered them fully. Joseph Smith’s history says that soon after, he tried to write a revelation and failed (67). Section 68 sends him to preach, and section 75 revokes his eastern mission and rebukes him for murmuring. He later recalled how the preface (section 1) was produced.
connections: His missionary companions in these sections were Samuel H. Smith and Luke Johnson. He was called to the Twelve with Lyman Johnson, Orson Hyde, and others in 1835.

sources.title: William E. McLellin, Joseph Smith Papers biography

reviewNote: JSP: born 18 Jan. 1806, Smith County, Tennessee; baptized 20 Aug. 1831 in Jackson County; excommunicated 3 Dec. 1832 and apparently reinstated; apostle 15 Feb. 1835; excommunicated 1838; later joined several other movements; died 14 Mar. 1883, Independence. Section 118 does not name him; its setting mentions him among the fallen.
